subject: Request: DPA amendment — training prohibition, ephemeral KV residency, and subprocessor notice window
messages:
From: Claudia Ramos <claudia@careclear.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: tom.ellis@careclear.com, LegalOps <legalops@careclear.com>
Date: 2025-07-28T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: DPA redlines and operational asks (training prohibition + residency)

Hi Stephanie,

Thanks again for the demo last week. Our legal and security teams reviewed the DPA and we've attached a redline (CareClear_DPA_redlines_20250728.pdf). The main asks are: 

- Explicit prohibition on model improvement/training with customer data (we're asking for a short clause: "Customer Data will not be used to improve or train vendor models").
- Clear ownership of prompts and generation outputs (CareClear retains all rights to prompts and outputs).
- Ephemeral KV / prefix caching only — we need a config and retention guarantee (max 24 hours) and proof of deletion procedures.
- Geo-locked backups and onshore KMS for any exported material.
- 30-day advance notice for adding subprocessors, and a right to object for high-risk subprocessors.

Could you confirm operational feasibility and provide evidence (SOC2 snapshot or an ops note) that maps these asks to your platform capabilities? We're on a tight timeline for procurement (week of Aug 4).

Appreciate it — happy to hop on a call if that's easier.

Best,
Claudia Ramos
Head of Security & Privacy
CareClear Health

Attachments: CareClear_DPA_redlines_20250728.pdf

From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com>
To: Claudia Ramos <claudia@careclear.com>
Cc: kimberly_park@redwood.com, david_kim@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2025-07-28T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redlines and operational asks (training prohibition + residency)

Hi Claudia — thanks for the clear summary and the redline. Looping in Kimberly (legal) and David (infra/ops) to confirm feasibility and what evidence we can share.

Quick notes from my side:
- We can commit contractually to a no-training clause for customer-specific workloads (we'll propose wording Kimberly can sign off on).
- Ephemeral KV retention as a configurable policy is supported by our runtime; need David's note on retention enforcement and deletion proofs.
- Onshore KMS and geo-locked export lanes are available via our Private offering; there are a few implementation options (region pin vs. on-prem key).
- Subprocessor notification windows are usually 30 days for major changes; there is an "objection" path for specified high-risk subprocessors.

I'll share a short ops summary and the SOC2 snapshot as attachments this afternoon. If you prefer, we can schedule a 30-minute call to run through redlines.

Next step: Kimberly will propose contract language, David will provide an ops attachment mapping items to controls, and I'll set up the call if helpful.

Thanks,
Stephanie
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redline_DPA_Stephanie_v1.pdf

From: kimberly_park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: Claudia Ramos <claudia@careclear.com>, david_kim@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2025-07-28T13:20:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redlines and operational asks (training prohibition + residency)

Claudia / team — thanks for the redline. I've reviewed the PDF and made a couple of suggestions in the attached redline (Redline_DPA_Stephanie_v1.pdf). High-level:

- "No-training" clause: we can accept a scoped contract clause preventing Redwood from using CareClear-provided customer data to train or improve Redwood's general models. We'll need an explicit carveout allowing metrics/telemetry for platform reliability (non-content, aggregated) — I'll propose language.
- Prompts/outputs: we can grant ownership of prompts and outputs back to CareClear; we'll add standard language clarifying derivative rights (no transfer of Redwood IP).
- Subprocessor notice: 30 days is acceptable; we will include a defined objection process (90-day remediation + substitution or termination right).

Operational evidence: David, can you prepare:
  1) a 1-page ops note on ephemeral KV enforcement and deletion proofs (what logs we provide),
  2) SOC2 snapshot (redacted) and the KMS/residency diagram,
  3) outline of how we handle subprocessor notifications and a sample notice email.

If CareClear needs escrow for model outputs, we can discuss an addendum; otherwise the redline with the proposed language should be review-ready.

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachments: (see earlier)

From: david_kim <david_kim@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Cc: Claudia Ramos <claudia@careclear.com>, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: 2025-07-29T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Re: DPA redlines and operational asks (training prohibition + residency)

Team / Claudia — technical summary below, attaching the ops note (ephemeral_kv_config_summary.pdf) and a redacted SOC2 snapshot (SOC2-snapshot-2025Q1.pdf).

1) Ephemeral KV / caching
- Architecture: KV entries are tagged per-tenant; TTL enforcement happens at the runtime and is backed by deletion jobs.
- Configurable retention: we can set a tenant policy of 24 hours maximum.
- Proof of deletion: we can provide deletion job logs (timestamped) and audit entries. We cannot provide raw deleted content, but we can provide hashes and retention timestamps.

2) Onshore KMS + geo-locking
- We offer customer-managed keys in supported regions; for CareClear we can route exports through an onshore KMS and ensure backups remain in US regions only.
- For highest assurance, we can support a private deployment with dedicated GPUs and a pinned region.

3) Subprocessor notifications
- We publish subprocessor lists and send email notices 30 days prior to changes for high-impact subprocessors; low-impact updates are posted in the portal with a 14-day notice.
- Objection handling: we support a remediation window and either replace the subprocessor or provide a migration path.

Attachments: ephemeral_kv_config_summary.pdf, SOC2-snapshot-2025Q1.pdf

If CareClear requires a short call to walk through diagrams, happy to do that later this week.

-David
David Kim
Director, Infrastructure & Ops, Redwood Inference

- Can you share a sample subprocessor notice and the portal location?
- For deletion proofs, hashes + timestamps are acceptable. We'll want SFTP or API access to exports for escrow if we exercise that option.
- If possible, please add the proposed contract language for the "no training" clause into the redline so our legal ops can compare directly.

If you send a DocuSign-ready redline (or a short call tomorrow at 10am PT), we can try to close this week and get to signature.

Thanks,
Tom Ellis
Sr. Director, Procurement
CareClear Health
